Schedule hands-on Dedicated benchmarking session (SE + Citadel infra)
Provide retention and deletion policy examples and pricing impact appendix

Liam Ortiz | Prepare Dedicated benchmark runbook and request sample prompts & seq lengths | 2027-02-16

meeting_header:
Date: 2027-02-09 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Derek Ramos (Redwood SE), Paula Reyes (CISO, Citadel), Mark Liu (Head ML Eng), Sara Patel (Infra Lead), Jonah Kim (Procurement)
summary: Intro discovery focused on security posture across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options. Customer (Citadel) prioritized strong encryption, KMS control, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit logs. Discussed SOC2/ISO evidence, data residency and retention requirements, and next steps to run Dedicated benchmarks and share security artifacts.
topics: SOC2 and ISO attestations; SSO/SAML and SCIM; RBAC and least privilege; audit logging and log export; encryption at rest and in transit (KMS/HSM options); data retention and deletion SLA; hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs; benchmarking and pilot scope
transcript:
00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood, I work on the enterprise AE team. Quick roll call?
00:07 Paula: Paula here, CISO at Citadel.
00:09 Mark: Mark, ML lead.
00:11 Sara: Sara, infra.
00:12 Jonah: Jonah, procurement.
00:13 Liam: Liam Ortiz, SE from Redwood.
00:15 Derek: Derek on the SE bench today.
00:17 Maya: Awesome. Today we wanted to focus on security posture and how Redwood fits into Citadel's compliance and ops requirements, especially as you evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
00:28 Paula: Yeah main thing for us is control over keys and auditability. We operate in regulated finance, so SOC 2 Type II is baseline and we're asking for ISO 27001 as well. We also need SSO with SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC controls, and pretty strict data retention and deletion policies.
00:42 Maya: Totally, that's the typical checklist. We have SOC2 and ISO attestations and can share the PDFs. For keys, Hosted can use Redwood-managed KMS, Dedicated gives customer-provided KMS via cloud KMS integrations, and Private on-prem lets you control HSM if needed.
00:58 Mark: When you say "Dedicated gives customer-provided KMS", do you mean we can attach our AWS KMS key to the dedicated pool or is that only in Private?
01:06 Liam: Good question. For Dedicated we support customer KMS where the key lives in your cloud account — you can bring your own key (BYOK) and we encrypt model cache and persisted artifacts with that KMS. For Private, obviously control is in your VPC/on-prem and you can use HSMs as well.
01:20 Sara: Any audit log exports? We need immutable logs shipped to our SIEM and retention for 7 years for some of our data.
01:27 Derek: Yes, we stream audit logs — both admin plane and user request logs — to customer destinations like S3, GCS, or direct syslog/Splunk. You can configure retention on your side. For Hosted we retain short-term logs for debugging but long-term retention is customer-managed via export.
01:41 Paula: Are there any gaps for hosted where Redwood still has access to raw inputs? We can't have any uncontrolled data residency or data access by third parties.
01:49 Maya: On Hosted, we do process inputs in our multi-tenant environment; we have strict controls, data segregation, and contractual commitments. We also offer an option to disable data usage for model training and persistent telemetry. But for high assurance customers we recommend Dedicated or Private to get isolation and BYOK.
02:04 Mark: What's the difference in latency/cost if we go Dedicated vs Hosted — because for ML ops pipeline, inference latency matters and we might prefer some cache behavior.
02:12 Liam: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency because it's single-tenant GPU pools; you also get more control over batching/kvar cache parameters. There's an upfront commitment cost but unit token cost can be lower at scale. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and great for evals.
02:28 Paula: Back to compliance — can you share the SOC2 report and ISO certificate?
02:32 Maya: Yes — I'll send the attestation PDFs after the call.
02:35 Jonah: Also need the standard DPA and security questionnaire filled.
02:38 Maya: We'll fill in your standard security questionnaire and send the DPA.
02:41 Sara: About SAML — our IdP is Okta. Does Redwood support SAML assertion mapping to groups and SCIM provisioning?
02:49 Liam: Yes we support SAML assertion with group mappings; SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle; RBAC can be mapped to Okta groups and we also have roles within the console.
02:58 Paula: Are there fine-grained roles for auditor vs developer vs admin?
03:03 Derek: Yes, we have predefined roles and you can create custom roles with least-privilege permissions. All actions are recorded in audit logs.
03:10 Mark: How are embeddings and PII handled? We sometimes send customer PII in prompts (hashed etc). Need clarifications on retention and deletion.
03:19 Maya: We recommend tokenization and client-side hashing where possible. For retention, Hosted by default has ephemeral cache and you can opt out of logging of prompts; Dedicated/Private gives you full control — you can set the cache to not persist, set KV cache policies, and manage retention in your own environment.
03:33 Paula: Encryption at rest and in transit — what algorithms and HSM support?
03:38 Liam: TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 for at-rest encryption. For BYOK we integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault. Private/on-prem can integrate with external HSMs depending on your deployment. We also support customer-managed rotation schedules.
03:56 Jonah: Any penetration test or vuln scan reports we can get?
04:00 Maya: We have a summary pen test report and vuln management program details — I will include the summary and the process, though raw pen test reports might be shared under NDA.
04:10 Paula: Okay. For auditability we need end-to-end traceability: which user triggered request, model version, tokens generated, and the actions done in console. Do you record model versions and rollout changes?
04:22 Derek: Yes, we tie every request to a deployment id, model version, route config, and user identity when available. Rollouts and canary deployments are captured in the control plane and show up in audit logs and change history.
04:34 Sara: If we host in our VPC (Dedicated or Private), what's the network topology? Do you allow peering or private link?
04:42 Liam: Dedicated can be deployed into your VPC and we support AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering options; for Private on-prem we ship an appliance/runbook. We'll need your network diagram to propose specifics.
04:55 Mark: From an ML perspective, we want to run a benchmark of our prompts — sequence lengths vary but tail latency is important. What's the easiest path?
05:03 Liam: For benchmarking we can spin a Dedicated trial pool, run a set of workload prompts, monitor tokens/sec and p50/p95 latency, and capture costs. We'll need sample prompts and an expected concurrency profile.
05:14 Paula: Data residency — can we ensure data stays in specific regions?
05:18 Maya: Yes, you can constrain workloads to regions. Hosted has region options, Dedicated is region-local, Private is fully localized.
05:24 Jonah: Procurement question — what is the SLA and indemnity language for Dedicated/Private?
05:29 Maya: SLA is part of the dedicated contract — we provide uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated. We'll follow up with a redline and standard terms.
05:36 Paula: One more: do you support bring-your-own-model or only Redwood-curated models? We may want to host a fine-tuned internal model.
05:44 Liam: You can bring custom model artifacts for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports selected BYOM in some cases but Dedicated/Private is recommended for custom models due to isolation and performance tuning.
05:55 Mark: Any limitations on model sizes or GPU types?
05:58 Liam: We support a broad catalog; for very large models we recommend specific GPU families — we can share the quantization and kernel matrix.
06:08 Paula: Ok let's recap next steps.
06:10 Maya: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, pen test summary, DPA, and SSO integration guide. Liam will scope a Dedicated benchmark run and we'll get sample prompts from Mark. Sara will share KMS vendor and data retention policy. We'll aim to reconvene after they review — Derek and I will be on the benchmark call.
06:28 Paula: Sounds good.
06:30 Jonah: Thanks everyone.
06:32 Maya: Thanks all, I'll follow up with links and the security questionnaire.
06:35 [call ends]
notes: Customer is high priority lead in finance. Security is blocking for hosted option; customer leans toward Dedicated with BYOK and log exports. Procurement will want standard indemnity and SLA redlines. SE asked for prompts and concurrency to scope benchmark. Expect follow-up in 2 weeks.
